- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days; reduce initial values by 5–10% relative to historical mean.
- Underestimate sharp downward spikes (e.g., 34.33, 33.70) — adjust downward by 2–5% of the spike magnitude if preceded by a rise.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves (e.g., 44.49 → 44.18 → 41.16) — cap forecast at 10–15% below the peak if followed by a drop.
- Mean-revert toward 35–40 range after 10+ consecutive high values; apply exponential decay with λ=0.15.
- Lagged low values (e.g., 34.33, 33.70) are often missed — add 1–2 lagged low values to forecast if recent history shows volatility.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if last 5 days are above 42, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3 days.
- If true outcome shows “double dip” (e.g., 45.93 → 34.33 → 42.87), forecast should dip 5–8% below peak then rebound 3–5% above low.
